symptom: re-running a settled script of 600 `create or modify microflow` statements took 23 s on a project where creating them took 9 s; `check` of a 600-page script with no project took 4.5 s (ako/mxcli#2160)
cause: the parser ran in ANTLR's default prediction mode (LL): SLL first, and full-context prediction wherever SLL sees a conflict. That second decision is not cached in the DFA, and on this grammar it was taken for nearly every statement: execATNWithFullContext was 10.5 s of the 13.1 s spent in visitor.Build. The re-run shows it most because `create or modify` of an existing flow describes the stored flow and parses the description to compare it with the statement, in the check and again in the exec: two parses per statement, about 9 ms each for 25 lines
insight: Found by timing a re-run after a first run, which no measurement of this issue had done for microflows on a seeded project: the stages were always profiled creating. The profile said 'planFlowModify 42%', which reads as a modify-path problem; one level down it was 90% visitor.Build, a cost every command pays. Two-stage parsing is ANTLR's documented remedy and its safety is one-directional: SLL accepting implies the LL tree, SLL rejecting implies nothing, so an SLL error means parse again and take the second parse's tree and messages. The Go runtime's BailErrorStrategy panics 'implement me' on an inline recovery, so stage one runs to the end with the ordinary error listener and is discarded if it recorded anything. Compared with full LL alone on every script under mdl-examples whole and cut off at two thirds: 2,584 inputs, 682 of them with errors, identical programs (reflect.DeepEqual) and identical messages. Measured, same machine, interleaved: microflow re-run 23.3 s -> 7.5 s, microflows first run 8.6 s -> 6.0 s, pages first run 33.0 s -> 28.8 s, entities 5.4 s -> 4.5 s, check of the page script 4.5 s -> 0.4 s. The same timing showed the settled page re-run at 109 s, which is not the parser (100 s after this) and is still open.
